items.title: Ex-pilot with drug record, foreign woman identified in Laos private jet drug trafficking probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian police have identified two Filipinos, including a former pilot, believed to be involved in an international drug trafficking syndicate linked to the seizure of more than half a tonne of methamphetamine aboard a private jet in Laos. Federal Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said investigations revealed that the former pilot had chartered the aircraft through a Malaysian broker, while other suspect, a woman, was believed to have acted as the syndicate's coordinator. Hussein said the latest findings followed investigations into the seizure at Luang Prabang International Airport in Laos, which also led to the detention of a Malaysian pilot.

items.title: Cross-border haze to ease in two weeks as monsoon transition begins, says deputy minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The cross-border haze that has affected Malaysia’s air quality since August 8 is expected to gradually subside over the next two weeks as wind patterns change, Deputy Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Syed Ibrahim Syed Noh said. He said Malaysia had entered the monsoon transition phase on October 9, with the northeast monsoon expected to begin towards the end of this month. Syed Ibrahim was responding to concerns raised by Khoo Poay Tiong (PH-Kota Melaka), who described the haze as a national crisis affecting public health, safety, the economy and public well-being.

items.title: Malaysia, China to step up cooperation against cyber scams, drug smuggling
items.summary: BEIJING: Cross-border investigations and the recovery of assets stolen through cyber scams are among Malaysia's key priorities in strengthening security cooperation with China, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. He said closer bilateral cooperation would help both countries tackle transnational crime while delivering practical benefits under their comprehensive strategic partnership, particularly in security and law enforcement. He said Malaysia and China were also strengthening intelligence sharing and coordinating investigations and enforcement operations to combat cross-border crime.

items.title: 492 foreign workers detained in Johor factory raid
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Some 492 foreign workers were detained and a factory manager arrested during an immigration raid at an automotive and electronics components factory in Tebrau, Johor. The manager was arrested for allegedly harbouring migrants. Johor Immigration director Datuk Mohd Rusdi Mohd Darus said the authorities had received a tip-off that the factory had allegedly hired migrants to keep operating costs low.

items.title: BYD expands Sarawak network with Miri 3S centre
items.summary: BYD Sime Motors has opened a new 3S centre in Miri, Sarawak, expanding its sales and aftersales network in the state as it builds up support for its electric vehicles (EVs). The 12,228 square feet (sq ft) facility is the company's largest 3S centre in Sarawak, combining vehicle sales, servicing and spare parts under one roof. The opening follows Sime Motors' establishment of East Malaysia's first BYD 3S centre in Kota Kinabalu in December 2024.

items.title: Haze: Kedah schools to operate as usual tomorrow as API readings remain moderate
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Oct 13 — All schools in Kedah will operate as usual tomorrow, with Air Pollutant Index (API) readings across the state remaining below 100 as of 2pm today. In a statement, the Kedah State Education Department (JPN) said any decisions on school closures or reopening due to the haze would be subject to the Education Ministry’s directives, based on JPN’s monitoring of daily API readings and local developments. “Kedah JPN will continue to monitor the situation and coordinate with the District Education Offices and schools to safeguard the health, safety and well-being of students and education personnel,” it added.

items.title: Home Ministry to seek details on five Malaysians held in Japan drug bust, says Saifuddin Nasution
items.summary: SUNGAI PETANI, Oct 13 — The Home Ministry will contact Japanese authorities to obtain accurate information on the arrest of Malaysians suspected of involvement in a drug case in Japan. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said he had instructed Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan to act immediately to establish the facts. However, he said destinations in Japan, including Tokyo, were not included in the original list of hotspots.

items.title: Kelantan prepares 451 evacuation centres ahead of monsoon
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Kelantan has prepared 451 temporary evacuation centres (PPS) with the capacity to accommodate 200,000 flood victims ahead of the coming northeast monsoon. State Social Welfare Department director Che Samsuzuki Che Noh said the centres were located across all districts, with most in Pasir Mas and Tumpat. He said 162 forward bases had also been set up as part of the state's flood preparedness measures.

items.title: Businessman sentenced to six months’ jail, ordered to pay RM5,000 for assaulting ex-girlfriend
items.summary: Magistrate Amira Sariaty Zainal imposed the sentence on Hoh Peng Onn, 47, after the defence failed to raise reasonable doubt at the end of the defence case. The accused must also pay RM5,000 in compensation to the victim, taking into account the trauma, injuries and emotional distress she suffered,” Amira Sariaty said. The court also ordered that Hoh serve an additional two months in jail if he failed to pay the compensation today.

items.title: Maybank lawsuit reinstated: Court orders trial over unauthorised RM60k transfer
items.summary: The Johor Baru High Court ruled that Wong Bair Lim's allegations of negligence and unauthorised online transfers raised issues that could only be resolved through a full trial. Judicial commissioner Noradura Hamzah said the Sessions Court had erred in dismissing Wong's lawsuit without properly examining the disputed facts. These included whether Wong had authorised the transactions and whether the bank had taken adequate steps to prevent possible fraud.

items.title: Onn Hafiz: Johor's 8pc growth no reason for complacency
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Johor must turn its strong economic growth and investment inflows into high-paying jobs for locals and greater opportunities for small businesses, said Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi. Onn Hafiz said investments, particularly through the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ), must create more high-income employment for locals, help small and medium enterprises expand and ensure balanced and sustainable development. He said that leadership required integrity, fairness and sincerity, adding that leaders must lead by example and ensure policies deliver tangible benefits to the people.

items.title: The guest that came early and we don't really know what to do
items.summary: IN September 2026, something pivotal happened to the Malaysian automotive landscape: the total number of battery electric vehicles cracked the 10 per cent mark, at least a year ahead of most optimistic predictions. Proton New Energy Technology, or Pro-Net - the subsidiary entrusted to explore the electrified market for the nation's oldest carmaker - reported achieving 20,000 total unit sales sometime in June. And so, in September, BEV sales hit 11 per cent.

items.title: Veterans who retired before 2013 still awaiting pension adjustments – Ketereh MP
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Veterans who retired before Jan 1, 2013, are still awaiting pension adjustments, leaving them receiving lower pensions than those who retired after that date, the Dewan Rakyat was told today. Datuk Khlir Mohd Nor (PN-Ketereh) said the disparity remained unresolved despite repeated appeals. Khlir said many of the affected veterans had served between 1946 and 1990 and were now aged 60 and above.

items.title: Haze forces school closures in 3 Pahang districts
items.summary: KUANTAN: Pekan will be the third district in Pahang, after Kuantan and Rompin, to close schools tomorrow due to worsening haze, the Pahang Education Department said. "The department prioritises the safety, health and well-being of students and teachers amid the current haze situation," it said. The department said the Sijil Tinggi Agama Malaysia (STAM) and Sijil Tinggi Persekolahan Malaysia (STPM) examinations would proceed as scheduled.

items.title: Budget 2027: Malaysia’s 3.3pc fiscal deficit target achievable, says Tengku Zafrul
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Malaysia is capable of achieving its fiscal deficit target of 3.3 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP) under Budget 2027, provided the assumptions underpinning the budget hold amid global economic and geopolitical uncertainties, said Datuk Seri Tengku Zafrul Abdul Aziz. He described Budget 2027 as a responsible budget that balances investment incentives with efforts to ensure that economic growth benefits a wider segment of Malaysians and businesses. On investment prospects, Tengku Zafrul said planned capital expenditure by government-linked investment companies (GLICs) and government-linked companies (GLCs) could generate positive spillover effects for the broader economy.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM OCT 13, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia extended its gains for a second consecutive session, with banking stocks leading advances among the FBM KLCI constituents. The benchmark index rose 0.33 per cent to close at 1,623 points, suggesting bargain hunting had emerged following last week's sell-off. In the cryptocurrency market, Bitcoin edged higher to RM341,036, while Ethereum rose to RM10,251.

items.title: Malaysian busted trying to smuggle 980 cigarette packs into Singapore
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: A Malaysian man's attempt to enter Singapore with duty-unpaid cigarettes hidden in his pickup truck's tyres came unstuck at Woodlands Checkpoint, where officers uncovered more than 980 boxes. The 31-year-old was arrested after Singapore Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) officers diverted his Malaysia-registered car for enhanced checks on Sept 26. ICA said its search and examination officers discovered the cigarettes concealed within the tyres.

items.title: Ringgit ends marginally lower against US dollar ahead of US inflation data
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit closed slightly lower against the US dollar on Tuesday as investors remained cautious ahead of the United States inflation data due tomorrow, an analyst said. At 6pm, the ringgit eased to 4.0835/0880 against the greenback from Monday's close of 4.0820/0865. TA Securities chief economist Shazma Juliana Abu Bakar said the data could influence expectations for the Federal Reserve's monetary policy direction and, consequently, near-term movements in the ringgit.

items.title: Lianson Fleet buys US$23mil bulk carrier
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Lianson Fleet Group Bhd has bought a Japanese-built bulk carrier for US$23 million or about RM93.9 million. This is part of Lianson Fleet's strategy to expand its marine transportation fleet and diversify beyond offshore support vessels. The company said the acquisition would strengthen its recurring income stream and improve earnings visibility, supported by the vessel's long-term charter potential and utilisation.

items.title: Dewan Rakyat: Pasir Mas, Jelutong MPs clash over Rohingya issue
items.summary: The argument broke out while Ahmad Fadhli Shaari (PN-Pasir Mas) was debating the budget, when RSN Rayer (PH-Jelutong) interjected and claimed that Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang (PN-Marang) and former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak had previously welcomed Rohingya refugees into Malaysia. Bachok, listen. Anwar.

items.title: 'Stingy newlywed': Syed Saddiq teased during Budget debate
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Newlywed Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman (Muda-Muar) was the subject of light-hearted teasing in the Dewan Rakyat today, just three days after marrying singer-actress Bella Astillah. Mohd Sany Hamzan (PH-Hulu Langat) jokingly called him a "pengantin kedekut" (stingy newlywed) when Syed Saddiq appeared reluctant to give way to an interjection during the 2027 Budget debate. "Stingy newlywed!"

items.title: Teen admits hitting grandmother with belt, threatening her with parang
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: An 18-year-old scrap metal collector pleaded guilty at the Yong Peng magistrate's court today to assaulting his 75-year-old grandmother with a belt and threatening her with a parang. Khairul Adam Yusof entered the plea after the two charges were read out before magistrate Mustaqim Sukarno. The second charge was under Section 506 of the Penal Code for criminal intimidation by pointing a parang at his grandmother.

items.title: Jati Tinggi banks on RM1.1bil orderbook amid share price weakness
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Jati Tinggi Group Bhd remains confident in its business outlook, citing an outstanding orderbook of about RM1.1 billion despite recent weakness in its share price amid volatility in technology and data centre-related stocks. The power infrastructure engineering group said there had been no material changes to its business operations or ongoing project execution arising from the recent market volatility. The group operates in the power infrastructure engineering sector, undertaking underground cable installation, overhead transmission line construction, substation works and other related electrical infrastructure projects.

items.title: Senior govt agency official, company director remanded seven days in bribery probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — A senior official of a government agency and a company director have been remanded for seven days for allegedly soliciting and receiving bribes totalling about RM15,000. Magistrate Aliaa Anwar issued the remand order against both men, effective from today until Oct 19, following an application by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) at the Kuala Lumpur Magistrate’s Court this morning. Meanwhile, Kuala Lumpur MACC director Mohammad Zakkuan Talib, when contacted, confirmed the remand.

items.title: Man jailed 30 years, handed 15 strokes for sexually assaulting daughter
items.summary: MUAR: An unemployed man was sentenced to 30 years in prison and 15 strokes of the rotan after pleading guilty to three charges of sexually assaulting his 14-year-old daughter. Sessions Court judge Emelia Kaswati Mohamad Khalid handed down the sentence today, citing the seriousness of the offences, which took place on separate occasions between Oct 3 and 5 at a house in a settlement in Segamat. The man was charged under Section 14(b), read together with Section 16 of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017.

items.title: Tokyo cocaine smuggling bust: Malaysia seeking info from Japanese authorities
items.summary: SUNGAI PETANI: The Home Ministry is seeking further information from Japanese authorities following the detention of five Malaysians suspected of attempting to smuggle about five kilogrammes of cocaine into Tokyo. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said accurate information was needed to establish the facts surrounding the incident, including how the group allegedly passed security checks at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) before being detained in Japan. He said he had instructed Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan to contact Japanese authorities to obtain more information.

items.title: RedPlanet IPO oversubscribed 85 times
items.summary: The enterprise information and communications technology solutions provider said it received 7,031 applications for 1.77 billion issue shares worth RM336.72 million from the public. The IPO involves issuing 70 million new shares and offering 10 million existing shares for sale through private placement to selected investors. It comprised 11.53 million new shares for selected investors, 18.22 million new shares for Bumiputera investors approved by the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry, and 10 million existing shares for selected investors.

items.title: MEF warns RM3,100 minimum wage could hurt small businesses
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A proposed RM3,100 minimum wage could discourage entry-level hiring and burden small businesses, the Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) said. MEF senior adviser for government, media and international engagement Datuk Dr Syed Hussain Syed Husman said wage decisions must be evidence-based and economically sustainable. Syed Hussain said wage proposals must account for differences in employers' ability to absorb higher costs, particularly among micro, small and medium enterprises.

items.title: STAM and MUET examinations in Pahang to continue as planned despite haze
items.summary: KUANTAN, Oct 13 — The Sijil Tinggi Agama Malaysia (STAM) and Malaysian University English Test (MUET) examinations in Pahang will proceed as scheduled despite the haze. In a statement, the Pahang State Education Department (JPN) said the examinations would be conducted in accordance with the standard operating procedures (SOP) and safety measures in force. Pahang JPN will continue to monitor the situation in coordination with the three district education offices and relevant agencies to safeguard the health, safety and well-being of students and education personnel.

items.title: Lorry driver in 12-vehicle crash pleads not guilty to drug-impaired driving
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: A 51-year-old lorry driver pleaded not guilty to driving under the influence of drugs, driving against traffic, and injuring four people on Oct 9. Deputy Public Prosecutor (DPP) Alia Anisa Khairus Masnan asked for RM15,000 bail for the traffic offence and requested the court to impound the accused's driving licence. Magistrate Ameera Mastura Khamis granted RM9,000 bail for the first charge and suspended Agilan's driving licence until the case concludes.

items.title: Teachers union: RM69b education allocation must bring real improvements to Malaysian schools
items.summary: West Malaysia Malay Teachers Union (KGMMB) president Dr Mohd Sobri Yusuf said the RM69 billion allocation, up from RM66.2 billion this year, should translate into meaningful improvements in schools, with its success measured by the actual benefits delivered to teachers and students. Mohd Sobri said the higher school maintenance allocation, which has doubled to RM2 billion, could deliver direct benefits to school communities, particularly in ensuring that learning facilities were safe and comfortable. Mohd Sobri said the recruitment of 200 teaching assistants for primary schools with large numbers of pupils could help reduce teachers’ workload, allowing them to focus more on teaching and students’ learning needs.

items.title: [UPDATED] MyEG Group companies under probe over RM230.9mil untransferred government revenue
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police have launched an investigation into the failure to transfer more than RM230.9 million in government revenue collections involving two companies under the MyEG Group. Federal Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID) director Datuk Rusdi Mohd Isa said the investigation involved MY E.G. Sdn Bhd and Zetrix AI Berhad following a police report lodged on Oct 7.

items.title: Experts urge 'immediate changes' to prevent rogue AI
items.summary: PARIS: More than 200 artificial intelligence and cybersecurity researchers called Tuesday for immediate action to prevent further cases of AI models going rogue and posing a risk to critical infrastructure. The letter signed by luminaries in the field including Nobel-prize winner Geoffrey Hinton and Turing Award winner Yoshua Bengio – both seen as godfathers of AI – called for models relating to cybersecurity be physically cut off from the internet during testing. Their letter called for organisations developing, deploying, and testing cyber-capable AI models be air-gapped – that is physically cut off from the internet – to ensure they do not escape.

items.title: Fahmi proposes initiative to preserve speeches, writings of Malaysia’s founding leaders
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil today has proposed a national initiative to preserve and revive historical speeches and writings of Malaysia’s founding leaders for future generations. He said the initiative, inspired by the reprint of pioneering journalist J. Victor Morais’ Great Wisdom of the First Malaysians, could involve retrieving rare speeches, writings and historical accounts from archives. Fahmi said this at the launch of Great Wisdom of the First Malaysians – A Reprint of Selected Speeches by Pioneering Journalist J. Victor Morais here today.

items.title: 2027 Budget debate: Bachok MP calls for fixed federal-state revenue sharing formula
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The success of the 2027 Budget depends on closer cooperation between the federal and state governments, with states given greater flexibility to determine their development priorities, said Bachok member of parliament Mohd Syahir Sulaiman. Speaking during the 2027 Budget debate in the Dewan Rakyat today, he called for a fixed revenue-sharing formula that recognised states' contributions and faster implementation of federal projects, particularly in rural areas. Syahir said demands concerning petroleum, taxation and development allocations should be resolved fairly, particularly those involving Sabah, Sarawak, Kelantan and Terengganu.

items.title: Iskandar Puteri council nabs five strays following dog attacks
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI: The Iskandar Puteri City Council (MBIP) has caught five stray dogs following reports of dog attacks in Lima Kedai yesterday. Kota Iskandar assemblyman Datuk Pandak Ahmad said the operation would continue in a bid to protect residents, particularly children in residential areas. "Stray dogs pose a potential threat to residents, especially children playing in housing areas," Pandak said.

items.title: Boy attacked by pack of stray dogs while out buying medicine
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: A 15-year-old boy who was fleeing a pack of strays was bitten by one of the dogs at Perumahan Rakyat Lima Kedai yesterday. The pack, he said, immediately chased him. Aliff said this was his first time being attacked by dogs, and said it left him traumatised.

items.title: Kelantan breaks new ground with RM35mil social sukuk, Malaysia's first by state agency
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Permodalan Kelantan Bhd has issued RM35 million in social sukuk, marking Malaysia's first such issuance by a state agency and the first in Kelantan. The issuance was made under its RM300 million sukuk Wakalah, following its inaugural RM265 million sukuk issuance in November 2025, which was also the first sukuk in Kelantan. Permodalan Kelantan chairman Datuk Ahmad Yaakob said the issuance would provide an important source of financing to expand the company's Ar-Rahn Islamic pawnbroking business and widen access to Islamic financial services.

items.title: Middle East LNG industry remains hostage of Iran war
items.summary: WHILE Middle Eastern oil exports have rebounded in recent weeks, Qatar's vast liquefied natural gas export facilities remain hobbled. Qatar is the world's second-largest producer of LNG behind the United States. The severe disruption to Qatar's LNG exports, alongside a drop in exports from neighbouring United Arab Emirates, has sent shockwaves through global gas markets.

items.title: Orang Asli children should not be denied documentation over parents’ marriage records, says National Registration Dept
items.summary: GUA MUSANG, Oct 13 — Orang Asli children should not be left without documentation because of issues involving their parents’ marriage records, said National Registration Department (JPN) director-general Datuk Badrul Hisham Alias. He said JPN would assess each case based on the facts, supporting documents and individual circumstances to determine the appropriate action, particularly for birth registration. He said 143 New Generation MyKads had been issued to the Orang Asli community in Kelantan through the MEKAR Programme, which brings registration services closer to the community.

items.title: Body wrapped in cloth found in drain at Sama Gagah market in Penang
items.summary: Penang Police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng, when contacted by Bernama, confirmed the discovery and said investigations were underway to determine the circumstances surrounding the incident and the cause of death. Several photographs showing the body had earlier gone viral on social media. — Bernama

items.title: MACC records RM1.27b in asset freezes from 2022 to September, says deputy minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) recorded asset freezes worth RM1.27 billion from 2022 to September this year, involving bank accounts, jewellery, immovable property and other valuables. Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) M. Kulasegaran said the asset freezes were carried out under Section 44 of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (Act 613). He said 1,336 asset-freezing orders were issued under the Act in 2025, while another 1,006 were issued from Jan 1 to Sept 30 this year.

items.title: Budget 2027 should accelerate transition from R&D to Malaysian technology, says Mimos
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The government’s continued focus on strengthening the technology and innovation ecosystem through Budget 2027 provides an opportunity to accelerate the transition from research and development (R&D) to commercialisation, industry adoption and tangible economic value, said Mimos Bhd (Mimos). It said the government’s commitment to advancing Malaysia’s technology and innovation agenda, particularly through the Finance Ministry (MOF) and Science, Technology and Innovation Ministry (Mosti), would help strengthen the country’s R&D capabilities, develop home-grown technologies and translate innovation into economic and social benefits. Mimos President and Group Chief Executive Officer Dr Saat Shukri Embong said the next step for Malaysia is to ensure that these capabilities translate into commercial outcomes, stronger Malaysian intellectual property (IP), industry adoption and economic value.

items.title: Ministry to ensure Budget 2027 funds benefit women, children, OKU and elderly, says Nancy Shukri
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development’s (KPWKM) increased allocation under Budget 2027 will strengthen social protection and the well-being of target groups, including women, children, persons with disabilities (OKU) and the elderly. Its minister, Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri, said the funding, which rose four per cent to RM4.355 billion, would support various aid initiatives, the development of a care ecosystem and economic empowerment to help target groups realise their potential and become self-reliant. Nancy said the ministry is also focusing on women’s economic empowerment through an approach that combines skills, capital or equipment assistance, support networks and market opportunities to help them generate income.

items.title: Johor records nearly 10,000 commercial crime cases with RM212.64m in losses, says state top cop
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 13 — Johor police opened 9,897 investigation papers involving commercial crimes in the first nine months of this year, with losses totalling RM212.64 million. Its chief, Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad, said the figure represented an increase of 3,036 cases from the 6,861 recorded during the same period last year, although financial losses declined from RM252.57 million. Ab Rahaman said the state’s crime index also rose to 4,343 cases during the same period, compared with 4,152 last year.

items.title: King attends pre-council meeting of Conference of Rulers at Istana Negara
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, today attended the pre-council meeting of the 273rd Conference of Rulers at Istana Negara. According to a post on Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar’s Facebook page, the pre-council meeting was also attended by Tunku Temenggong Johor Tunku Idris Iskandar Al-Haj as the official representative of Johor Regent Tunku Mahkota Ismail. The 273rd Meeting of the Conference of Rulers will run for two days starting tomorrow and will be presided over by the Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Shah.

items.title: MetMalaysia warns of severe storms across peninsula and East Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning across several states in Peninsular Malaysia, Sarawak, and Sabah, forecasting heavy downpours, lightning, and gusty winds until 6pm today. In Kedah, stormy conditions are expected across eight districts: Langkawi, Kubang Pasu, Padang Terap, Sik, Baling, Kuala Muda, Kulim, and Bandar Baharu. In Perak, the warning covers Kerian, Larut, Matang dan Selama, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang, and Perak Tengah.

items.title: Molotov cocktail attack on Kulai Rohingya settlement linked to provocative viral clip, police say
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 13 — Police believe an early morning arson attack targeting several homes at an ethnic Rohingya settlement in Kulai Besar was triggered by racially provocative videos circulating on social media. “Police have also received a report on the incident at 1.30am,” he said in a statement today. Ab Rahaman said police have launched investigations under both anti-arson statutes and cyber-crime laws.

items.title: Miri-Subang flights to begin Dec 1, offering new link to Klang Valley
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Miri residents will have another air travel option when a new flight service to Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport (LTSAAS) in Subang begins operations on December 1, 2026. Deputy Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Chiew Choon Man said the new route would benefit residents who frequently travel for work, business, education, medical treatment and family commitments. He said improved air connectivity could benefit the business and tourism sectors while making travel between Miri and the Klang Valley more convenient.

items.title: Deputy minister: Anti-scalping provisions to be added to Price Control Act
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living is “actively” working on a dedicated legal framework to combat ticket scalping, with new regulations expected to take effect as early as next year, Parliament was told this morning. Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Deputy Minister Datuk Fuziah Salleh said anti-scalping provisions could be inserted under Section 15(1) of the Price Control and Anti-Profiteering Act, which grants authority to introduce measures curbing unfair pricing and resale practices. Fuziah said the anti-scalping provisions would include the definition of scalping itself, how to control bulk ticket purchasing activities and enforcing the use identification or names on ticket purchases.

items.title: Penang’s Jalan Magazine slip road to face periodic closures from Oct 14 until Feb 21 next year for Mutiara Line LRT works
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 13 — Part of the route along Jalan Magazine here will be closed periodically for 131 days starting tomorrow to make way for construction work on the Mutiara Line Light Rail Transit (LRT) Project. In a statement today, Malaysia Rapid Transit Corporation Sdn Bhd (MRT Corp) said the long-term closure will start from 10am tomorrow and continue until 5am on February 21, 2027. MRT Corp said the closure will facilitate construction work on the Mutiara Line LRT Project under Package CMC1, including road widening and utility relocation works.

items.title: Malaysia’s semiconductor exports remain exempt from US tariffs, says Johari Ghani
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Malaysia continues to enjoy tariff exemptions for its semiconductor exports to the United States, said Investment, Trade and Industry Minister (Miti) Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani. He said negotiations with the US under Section 301 covered four issues, namely forced labour, excess production capacity, the environmental standards and government subsidies. We do not have excess capacity,” said Johari.

items.title: Fadhlina: Schools in Johor, Melaka, Negeri Sembilan and nine districts to close tomorrow as haze lingers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Schools in Johor, Melaka and Negeri Sembilan will stay closed tomorrow, Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek announced today, as haze continues to affect parts of the country. Schools under nine district education offices (PPD) in Selangor, Pahang, Sabah and Sarawak will also be shut. Today’s closures covered Johor, Melaka, Negeri Sembilan and Putrajaya, along with the Hulu Langat, Petaling Perdana, Kuala Langat and Sepang PPDs in Selangor and the Kuantan and Rompin PPDs in Pahang.

items.title: Zahid: Malaysia and China ramp up fight against cyber scams, cross-border crime
items.summary: BEIJING, Oct 13 — Cross-border investigations and the recovery of assets stolen through cyber scams are among Malaysia’s key priorities in strengthening security cooperation with China, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. He said closer bilateral cooperation would help both countries tackle transnational crimes while delivering practical benefits under their comprehensive strategic partnership, particularly in security and law enforcement. The Deputy Prime Minister said Malaysia and China were also strengthening intelligence sharing and coordinating investigations and enforcement operations to combat cross-border crime.

items.title: MetMalaysia: Super El Nino forecast for March-May 2027, temperatures could break Malaysia’s 40.1°C record
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 13 — Malaysia needs to brace itself for the Super El Niño phenomenon, which is expected to bring scorching weather between March and May next year, potentially breaking the country’s record high temperature of 40.1 degrees Celsius. Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said the country’s maximum temperature could exceed 41 degrees Celsius, based on analysis of the current intense El Niño phenomenon, alongside the impacts of climate change and global warming. “If we look at current climate change trends, the rate of temperature increase in the country is approximately 0.13 degrees Celsius per decade.

items.title: Asyraf says BN’s Melaka seat talks 90pc complete, urges trust in Muslim political pact
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Barisan Nasional (BN) is in the final stages of seat negotiations for the Melaka state election, with the coalition aiming to defend the 21 state constituencies it secured in the previous polls. Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the remaining deliberations focus on the seven remaining seats across the 28-seat state legislative assembly, with potential seat swaps actively under consideration, NST reported. “The negotiations have reached 90 per cent completion, with only 10 per cent remaining.

items.title: Lorry driver in Shah Alam 12-vehicle pile-up pleads not guilty to drug-impaired driving
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 13 — A lorry driver pleaded not guilty in the Magistrates’ Court here to driving against traffic under the influence of drugs and causing injuries to four other individuals last week. Agilan is accused of driving a lorry under the influence of methamphetamine and amphetamine, rendering him unable to control the vehicle and resulting in injuries to four individuals aged between 58 and 17. DPP Nur Amirah Zahari proposed bail of RM7,000, after which Rohan requested a minimum bail amount.

items.title: Malaysia cautious over proposal to co-chair The Hague Group, says Tok Mat
items.summary: Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said accepting the role would raise questions about Malaysia’s participation in international legal instruments, including the Rome Statute, which he said could potentially conflict with the Federal Constitution. He said the proposal followed Malaysia’s active involvement in the group, an international platform aimed at increasing pressure on Israel over the Palestinian issue. Mohamad said Malaysia had also joined South Africa as a co-sponsor at the recent United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) to intensify pressure on Israel, including efforts to bring the matter before the UN Security Council (UNSC).

items.title: BYD driver still hospitalised as probe into fatal Jalan Kuching crash involving five-year-old girl heads to DPP
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The driver of a BYD Seal involved in a six-vehicle collision that killed a five-year-old girl on Jalan Kuching is still receiving treatment at a private hospital. Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said investigations into the incident were ongoing, Kosmo! Online reported today.

items.title: Zara Qairina’s mother refused post-mortem despite being briefed, wanted immediate burial, inquest told
items.summary: Investigating officer Insp Wong Yew Zhung said he had informed and explained to Noraidah, 46, at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital that a post-mortem would be conducted to assist investigations into Zara Qairina’s death. I want to bury her (Zara Qairina) immediately.” Wong said Noraidah signed several documents on July 17, 2025, before Zara Qairina’s remains were handed over to the family for burial.
